sections.title: Playwright locators
sections.body:
## 5.1 Storytelling: A permanent address versus a live search instruction

Imagine you need to contact the current manager of a department.

One approach is to save the current manager's phone number.

Another approach is to search for whoever currently holds the manager role whenever you need them.

If the manager changes, the stored phone number may become outdated, while the search instruction can still identify the new manager.

Playwright's Locator works more like the second approach.

A Locator represents a way to retrieve elements from the page when an operation needs them.

```typescript
const button = page.getByRole("button", {
    name: "Send"
});
```

This creates a Locator object. It does not immediately perform a click.

Later:

```typescript
await button.click();
```

Playwright resolves the target and performs the operation.

## 5.2 Locator lifecycle

Locators are central to Playwright's automatic waiting and retryable operations. 

## 5.3 All important locator methods

| TypeScript | Python | Identifies elements by |
|--------|--------|--------|
| `getByRole()` | `get_by_role()` | Accessibility role and name |
| `getByText()` | `get_by_text()` | Text |
| `getByLabel()` | `get_by_label()` | Associated label |
| `getByPlaceholder()` | `get_by_placeholder()` | Placeholder |
| `getByTestId()` | `get_by_test_id()` | Test identifier |
| `getByAltText()` | `get_by_alt_text()` | Alternative text |
| `getByTitle()` | `get_by_title()` | Title attribute |
| `locator()` | `locator()` | CSS, XPath and other supported selectors |

We will now understand when to use each.

sections.title: getByText()
sections.body:
Use a text locator when the relevant identifying information is the element's textual content. HTML: ```html

Knowledge Base

Document uploaded successfully

Processing document ``` Python: ```python page.get_by_text( "Document uploaded successfully", exact=True ) ``` TypeScript: ```typescript page.getByText( "Document uploaded successfully", { exact: true } ); ``` Regular expression: ```python import re page.get_by_text( re.compile(r"uploaded successfully", re.I) ) ``` ```typescript page.getByText(/uploaded successfully/i); ``` Playwright normalizes whitespace during text matching. Use text locators for messages, labels displayed as text, paragraphs and similar content. When interacting with a button or link, a role locator with an accessible name is usually more expressive. ## 7.1 AI response assertion Python: ```python expect( page.get_by_text( "Answer generated successfully" ) ).to_be_visible() ``` TypeScript: ```typescript await expect( page.getByText( "Answer generated successfully" ) ).toBeVisible(); ``` For real LLM responses, avoid asserting exact generated prose unless it is genuinely part of the application's deterministic contract.

sections.title: getByLabel()
sections.body:
## 8.1 Understanding HTML labels

A label identifies an associated form control.

```html
<label for="question">
    Question
</label>

<input id="question" type="text" />
```

The `for` attribute connects the label to the input's ID.

Another valid association uses nesting:

```html
<label>
    Include citations
    <input type="checkbox" />
</label>
```

## 8.2 Python

```python
page.get_by_label("Question").fill(
    "What is RAG?"
)
```

## 8.3 TypeScript

```typescript
await page.getByLabel("Question").fill(
    "What is RAG?"
);
```

The locator can also use supported ARIA labeling relationships.

### Important password-field interview trap

HTML password inputs do not have the ordinary implicit `textbox` accessibility role.

Therefore, this may not locate the password input:

```typescript
page.getByRole("textbox", {
    name: "Password"
});
```

Prefer:

```typescript
page.getByLabel("Password");
```

This is also more expressive for form controls.

sections.title: getByPlaceholder(), getByTestId(), getByAltText() and getByTitle()
sections.body: ## 9.1 Placeholder locator HTML: ```html ``` Python: ```python page.get_by_placeholder( "Ask anything" ).fill("Explain agents") ``` TypeScript: ```typescript await page.getByPlaceholder( "Ask anything" ).fill("Explain agents"); ``` A placeholder is often less stable than an explicit label and should not substitute for accessible labeling in the application itself. ## 9.2 Test ID locator HTML: ```html ``` Python: ```python page.get_by_test_id( "generate-answer" ).click() ``` TypeScript: ```typescript await page.getByTestId( "generate-answer" ).click(); ``` Test IDs create an explicit contract between the frontend and automation framework. They are particularly useful when visible text changes frequently, multiple controls have similar names or the UI supports multiple languages. ## 9.3 Customize the test ID attribute Suppose your company uses: ```html ``` Python: ```python playwright.selectors.set_test_id_attribute( "data-qa" ) ``` TypeScript Playwright configuration: ```typescript import { defineConfig } from "@playwright/test"; export default defineConfig({ use: { testIdAttribute: "data-qa" } }); ``` Then continue using the normal test ID locator methods. ## 9.4 Alternative text locator HTML: ```html ``` Python: ```python page.get_by_alt_text( "Agent architecture diagram" ) ``` TypeScript: ```typescript page.getByAltText( "Agent architecture diagram" ); ``` ## 9.5 Title locator HTML: ```html Running ``` Python: ```python page.get_by_title("Execution status") ``` TypeScript: ```typescript page.getByTitle("Execution status"); ``` ## 9.6 Interactive locator selection laboratory ## Choose a locator for a UI element Target elementCurrent selection unavailable.Locator strategy Element attributes Predefined demonstration elements, not a live HTML locator engine. ## 9.7 Recommended locator selection order This is a practical heuristic, not a mandatory ordering. A stable test ID may be the best choice for certain applications.
